cards.front: What did Hermann Ebbinghaus publish in 1885?
cards.back: He published a book about his experiments on memory and forgetting.

cards.front: What happens to memory right after learning according to the forgetting curve?
cards.back: Memory fades fastest right after learning, and the rate of forgetting slows down as time goes on.

cards.front: What did the 2006 study by Roediger and Karpicke find about retrieval practice versus rereading?
cards.back: Rereading scored slightly higher right after studying, but one week later the group that practiced recalling remembered more.

cards.front: Why is finding concrete examples useful?
cards.back: It makes abstract ideas easier both to remember and to apply.
It is the ability to step back and examine your own thinking and know what you know and do not know.

cards.front: According to John Dunlosky and his colleagues in 2013, which two methods were rated as the most useful?
cards.back: Practice testing (retrieval practice) and distributed practice (spaced repetition).

cards.front: Why do researchers call difficult study methods desirable difficulties?
cards.back: Because they make learning feel slower in the moment while making memory stronger in the end.
